text:
alex: quick heads-up: found an odd interaction between the OTEL header-scrub hook and our retry wrapper in the Node sample app. looks like when the retry replays a request it sometimes reattaches X-Request-ID even though the inbound scrub removed it.

tara: ugh. do we see this in python too or only node?

alex: only observed in node so far. i ran the electron sample and the plain node sample. python-sdk seems to scrub+retry fine (probably because their retry reads headers from the live req object).

mike: can you share the minimal repro?

alex: yep — tiny repro below (local server + curl):
```
# start sample server with verbose logs
DEBUG=redwood:telemetry node samples/header-repro/server.js
# trigger auth failure that causes retry replay
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer invalid' http://localhost:4000/echo | cat -
```

alex: minimal log snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-22T20:11:03.001Z info telemetry inbound scrub X-Request-ID: <redacted>
2026-03-22T20:11:03.042Z warn auth auth-failed -> scheduling retry
2026-03-22T20:11:03.043Z debug retry replaying request headers: X-Request-ID=4a7b2c
2026-03-22T20:11:03.044Z info http response logged X-Request-ID=4a7b2c
```

tara: that debug line is the problem — retry is replaying the original header snapshot. does the retry wrapper stash headers on first attempt?

alex: yes, retry-wrapper keeps a cached copy of req.headers to speed replays. the scrub runs inside an OTEL inbound hook which mutates req.headers after the snapshot is captured. so the cached copy still has the sensitive id.

mike: thanks — that explains why python avoided it (their retry reads req.headers at replay time). could be an ordering/contract mismatch between our otel-shim and retry-wrapper.

devrel-bot: automated: security-notify: potential header leak when retry wrapper uses header-snapshots (see internal ticket RW-1089).

ops-oncall: if alerts start firing please set REDWOOD_REDACTION_VERBOSE=false to reduce noise and escalate.

alex: quick mitigations i tested: 1) change retry to snapshot later (just before sending) or better: snapshot from req.headers at replay time. 2) ensure redaction runs after all middleware that may mutate headers (move scrub to final outbound hook). 3) add a CI integration test that simulates auth failure+retry and scans logs for unredacted IDs. option (1) looked simplest and passed my local test.

tara: can you add the CI test to the sample-app repo? put it under tests/integration/telemetry-replay.spec.js and mark it flaky + skip on windows for now.

alex: yep will open a small PR with the test + the retry fix. PR will include: failing test first, then patch that updates retry to read headers at replay time, then test passing.

mike: please also add a unit test in node-sdk asserting that middleware ordering respects the OTEL scrub contract — that will catch future refactors.

alex: noted. i'll @mention eng-platform and add a short blurb to the release notes: "fix: ensure retry replays current request headers to avoid unredacted header replay".

ops-oncall: ping me when the alert triggers again and i'll mute the pager while y'all iterate.

tara: one more ask: can we add a telemetry-e2e hedged test that runs both node and python samples so we can catch disparity in SDK behavior? seems worth it given recent regressions.

alex: agree — will draft a ticket RW-1091 to add cross-sdk telemetry parity checks.

mike: thanks for the quick triage and the reproducible test - super helpful. :thumbsup:
